Guidance & calibrationthe arithmetic, in your browser

This is the guidance and calibration arithmetic only. There is no face recognition on this page, and none is being simulated.

The recogniser is a Haar cascade for detection and an LBPH model for matching, running in OpenCV against a 328 MB trainer.yml built from enrolled photographs, driven by a webcam the server owns. None of that fits in a tab, so none of it is here — there is no detector, no model, no camera and no identification. A page that mimed those would be telling you something untrue about the system it claims to demonstrate.

What is here is the two modules that import neither cv2 nor numpy, because they are arithmetic over numbers that something else measured: pipeline/guidance.py, which turns one frame’s measurements into the single instruction to show the person, and analysis/calibration.py, which turns a measured false-match table into the threshold a gallery of a given size can actually support. You supply the measurements with the sliders; the real engine gets them from the parts that are not here.

Guidance pipeline/guidance.py

Fourteen rules, tried in a fixed order; the first one that fires is the only thing the person is told. Move a slider past a threshold and watch which instruction takes over — the order is the design, so the chain below shows every rule that is firing, not just the winner.

      Calibration analysis/calibration.py

      A threshold swept on a small enrollment is misleading: with three people there are three ways to be wrong, so almost anything scores zero false matches. The table below was counted over , and the recommendation scales with how many people you have enrolled — that is the birthday problem, and it is why recommend_threshold takes a gallery size instead of returning a constant.

      These are impostor rates only. The corpus has one image per person, so it cannot measure the other half — a threshold that never confuses two people may also fail to recognise the right one. And the risk is not evenly shared: at threshold , of faces falsely match somebody against of faces, a × gap. SFace’s own published operating point is , which at any real gallery size is far too loose.
